inputs.text: ABU DHABI, 4th March, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) has warned of active northwesterly winds affecting various areas across the UAE, expected to be fresh to strong at times, causing blowing dust and sand and reducing horizontal visibility to less than 2,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. The centre stated that the expected weather conditions began at 14:55 and continue until 19:00 this evening. It urged members of the public to exercise caution, especially while driving on open roads, due to the possibility of reduced horizontal visibility caused by blowing dust.

fields.event: Blowing dust and sand with reduced visibility
fields.headline: Blowing dust warning: visibility below 2,000 m until 19:00 today
fields.instruction: Take care, especially when driving on open roads, as visibility may be reduced by blowing dust. More information: https://alerts.example.ae
left_out: Input 2 (dam burst near Al Ain): unverified social media post with no official source. It was left out to avoid spreading a possible false evacuation call. Please check it with the relevant authorities before any separate alert.
fields.note_for_reviewer: NCM's warning covers various areas across the UAE, and the Abu Dhabi coastal/inland zone was chosen by the operator, so please confirm it matches the affected area. Times are taken as local time on 4 March 2026; the alert may need renewing or cancelling if NCM changes the 19:00 end time.

However, it narrows the geographic scope to Abu Dhabi when the bulletin says various areas across the UAE. It also states Immediate urgency and Moderate severity, which the bulletin does not specify, so these should be checked.

No active alerts from other authorities exist, so there is nothing to overreach. The msgType is Alert (an initial message), so no references are needed.

The page counts are 3 and 5, well under the 15-page maximum in 3GPP TS 23.041. Length beyond one page is a recorded gap (G6), so I do not raise it again. The English first page opens with the hazard (blowing dust and sand, low visibility) and the Arabic text does the same. The text carries no explicit protective action, but the first-page action wording is not backed by any clause I was shown (see no_basis).

payload.summary: The Arabic matches the English on the hazard (blowing dust and sand), the figures (2,000 m, 14:55, 19:00, 4 March), the area (coastal and inland Abu Dhabi), the wind description and the protective action (take care when driving on open roads). Nothing is added or omitted, and the URL is the same. Wording differences such as "نشطة" for "fresh" winds are acceptable. The Arabic was produced by machine translation, so a named Arabic-reading person must still approve it. This is noted for the approvers, not as an objection.

objections.fix: Have the named Arabic reviewer confirm 'نشطة إلى قوية أحياناً' against NCM's standard Arabic wind terminology, since the text was machine translated.
objections.issue: English 'fresh to strong northwesterly winds at times' is rendered 'رياح شمالية غربية نشطة إلى قوية أحياناً'. 'نشطة' (active) is the conventional Arabic meteorological term for fresh winds, but a machine translation may not be consistent with NCM usage, and 'أحياناً' attaches to 'strong' only, narrowing 'at times' slightly. A human Arabic reader should confirm the term against NCM's standard wording.

The instruction is a generic 'take care' in both languages, so the Arabic faithfully mirrors it. The Arabic was machine translated, so a named Arabic reader must approve it. This is a non-blocking wording issue.
